answer_text:
Here's a breakdown of the maximum unemployment benefits you can collect in **Massachusetts** in 2026:

---

### 💰 Maximum Weekly Benefit
Your weekly benefit amount will be about **50% of your average weekly wage**, up to the maximum amount set by law. As of **October 5, 2025**, the maximum weekly benefit amount is **$1,105 per week**.

### 👨‍👧 Dependency Allowance
If you have dependents and you are their main support, you may be eligible for a **dependency allowance of up to $25 per child**. Spouses are not included.

### 📅 Maximum Duration
The **maximum duration of benefits is 30 weeks**. Under normal conditions, the duration is **26 weeks**.

### 💵 Maximum Total Payout
The total maximum payout — combining the weekly rate with the maximum duration — is approximately **$33,150** (30 weeks × $1,105).

### 📊 How It's Calculated
Unemployment benefits are calculated based on approximately **50% of your average weekly wage** during the base period. The base period is generally defined as the **first four of the last five completed calendar quarters** prior to the claim.

### 🏆 How Massachusetts Compares
Massachusetts is one of the most generous states in the country, with a maximum of **$1,105/week** (with dependents; **$823/week** without). It also provides the **longest duration** of any state, at up to **30 weeks**.

### 💼 Taxes
Unemployment benefits are **taxable** for both federal and Massachusetts state income tax purposes. You can elect to have **10% withheld for federal taxes** and **5% withheld for Massachusetts state taxes**.

---

For the most accurate and personalized estimate, you can use the benefit calculator at **mass.gov**.
